subject: Clarify: non-learning assurance + retention windows for logs/backups
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medicore.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medicore team is excited about the low-latency routing you showed. Before we proceed to procurement, our legal team wants a clear written assurance that Redwood will not use Medicore customer data to train models (or otherwise improve model weights). They also asked for specifics on retention windows for logs, backups, and snapshots (including any automated telemetry/metrics).

Concrete asks:
- A short, contract-ready sentence that says Redwood does not use Medicore data for training, with clear exceptions if any.
- What are the retention windows for request logs, KV cache snapshots, backups, and long-term analytics?
- Any circumstances where data might persist longer (e.g., legal hold, backups, monitoring dashboards)?
- Are aggregated/derived metrics used for model improvement? If so, are they impossible to link back to customers?

We appreciate a quick turn — procurement is trying to close by end of month.

Best,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Director, Platform & Security
Medicore

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medicore.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (Sales) and Marissa (Security & Privacy) so we can give you contract wording + tech details.

Short answers up front:
- Redwood does not use customer content to train or fine-tune our public models. We can include a contractual clause to that effect (draft attached).
- Operational telemetry and absolute request logs are retained on a configurable schedule; default production retention is 90 days for request logs, 30 days for KV cache snapshots, and 365 days for backups/snapshots that are part of disaster recovery.
- Exceptions: legal hold, compliance audits, or explicit customer opt-in. Backups are immutable for their retention window; we do purge expired backups per the retention schedule.
- Aggregated telemetry (latency histograms, token counts, failure rates) may be used internally for product improvement. We can provide an option to limit product-level analytics for enterprise customers under contract. Aggregated signals do not contain raw customer prompts or PII linking back to a single customer.

Next steps: Marissa will send precise definitions and the policy language we recommend for contract. Ben — can you confirm whether Medicore wants the no-training clause in Master Services Agreement or a side letter?

Cheers,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medicore.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Hi all — apologies for the delay, putting the technical/legal nuance here so Medicore legal has precise language. Attaching a short draft clause and a SOC2 summary (high level).

Draft clause (suggested):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content to train, improve, or fine-tune model weights for any public or commercial models without Customer's prior written consent. "

Definitions and exceptions (high-level):
- "Customer Content": data submitted by the Customer or end users of the Customer's applications to Redwood services.
- "Operational data": ephemeral logs, metrics, and telemetry generated by the service for debugging and improving reliability. By default, Redwood retains request logs for 90 days; KV cache snapshots for 30 days; DR backups for 365 days. These windows are configurable for enterprise customers via the Redwood Console and can be shortened by contract.
- "Backups and snapshots": backups used for disaster recovery are immutable during their retention window and will be purged after expiry. If Customer invokes a legal hold, Redwood will retain relevant backups until the hold is lifted; Redwood will notify Customer of the scope and duration of the hold.
- "Aggregated/derived metrics": Redwood may use non-identifiable, aggregated metrics (e.g., percentile latencies, token throughput) for product improvement; such usage will not contain prompt-level data or unique identifiers that can be traced to Customer.

Operational safeguards we enforce to make the above meaningful:
- Strict access controls and logging for engineers (RBAC + approval flow for any debug access).
- No data pipelines into model training clusters unless explicitly enabled via a documented opt-in process.
- Quarterly internal audits and SOC2 attestations covering access and retention policy.

If Medicore wants, we can add a short Service Level Exhibit that:
1) pins concrete retention windows in the contract,
2) provides an option to disable aggregated analytics for the account, and
3) commits to a maximum time-to-respond for legal holds.

Ben — re: commercial ask, Medicore is pushing for a contract-ready sentence plus retention numbers. I recommend we offer the standard retention windows as above and make shortened retention a committed term in the MSA for a small surcharge (per SecOps pricing).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medicore.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Alice — thanks for the patience. Medicore procurement asked that the sentence be in the MSA. We can add Marissa's clause into Section 7 (Data Use) and include an exhibit with the retention matrix. I'll have our contracts team prepare a redline by Thursday. Pricing note: the standard plan includes the retention windows above; if you require sub-30 day log retention or disabling aggregated analytics entirely, there will be a one-time onboarding change and a small monthly fee to cover increased SLO cost.

One more operational note: for Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can fully control retention via their deployment configuration. If Medicore is considering Dedicated capacity, we can include that as an alternative.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medicore.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligns with what we need. Medicore legal prefers the sentence in the MSA; they also asked that Redwood confirm in writing that aggregated metrics used for product improvement are de-identified and cannot be reconstituted to Customer Content. Can Marissa confirm that detail in the redline?

Assuming the redline includes Marissa's protections and the retention exhibit, Medicore legal is comfortable moving to signature.

Best,
Alice

Medicore
